origins: The need for control often grows in chaotic or frightening homes, where a child tried to bring order by managing everything around them. It can also follow trauma, a sudden loss, or a time when things spun out of control. Control can feel like safety. But because so much in life is beyond our control, this belief often leads to anxiety, tension in relationships, and exhaustion.
teaches: Scripture teaches that we can make plans, but the Lord directs our steps. James warns against confident boasting about tomorrow and teaches us to say, “If the Lord is willing.” God tells us to be still and know that He is God. Trusting the Lord with all our heart rather than leaning on our own understanding is not passivity; it is placing control in better hands. We are responsible for our choices, but the outcome belongs to God.
self_statements: If I don’t handle it, it will fall apart.
I can’t stand not knowing what will happen.
I have to plan for every possibility.
If I lose control, something bad will happen.
errors: Believing disaster will follow if I loosen my grip.
Insisting things must go my way.
Predicting that others will fail if I don’t manage them.
Thinking I can prevent outcomes that are really in God’s hands.
questions: When did I learn that I had to be in control?
What am I actually able to control, and what not?
What does my need for control cost me and others?
What happens when I try to control things I cannot?
What does God say about who directs my steps?
What is one thing I could release to God this week?
truth: I am responsible for my own choices, and I can plan wisely. But I cannot control everything, and I don’t have to. God directs my steps and holds what I cannot. I can do my part and trust Him with the rest.
hw_truths: I plan, and the Lord directs my steps.
I can be still and know He is God.
I am responsible for my choices, not every outcome.
Letting go is trusting, not giving up.
Worry cannot add an hour to my life.
log: Each day, write one thing you tried to control and one thing you chose to release to God.
actions: Draw a circle. Inside, write what you can control. Outside, write what you can’t. Pray over the outside list.
Let someone else do one task their way this week without correcting them.
Make one small plan with an open end, such as trying a new restaurant without reading reviews.
Each morning, name one worry and say, “Lord, I give this to You.”
prayer: Lord, I hold on so tightly because I am afraid. Thank You that You direct my steps and hold what I cannot. Help me do my part, release the rest, and rest in Your care. Amen.
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I must be in control.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
